goal: Review and lock the complete product contract for switchable, semantically equivalent layout profiles.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Requirements.md` and the client-facing layout terminology in `PRODUCT.md`, `docs/functionality/CLIENT-DESKTOP.md`, `apps/desktop/README.md`, and `apps/desktop/Design.md`. Context: the current code exposes two partial desktop shell strings while the requested product behavior covers complete desktop and mobile presentation systems. Target: confirm REQ-001 through REQ-014, users, workflows, scope, non-goals, and final acceptance without redefining feature capability or server policy. Design Considerations: keep profile identity semantic, separate user selection from responsive variants, and define capability parity across layouts. Design Value: a fixed product contract prevents renderer work from silently weakening state continuity or calling a shell-only change complete. Constraints & Risks: preserve the current client product boundary, do not add remote layout code, and update requirements before implementation if evidence changes the target.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md defines the user problem, desktop/mobile workflows, scope, non-goals, fourteen stable requirement labels, and one final acceptance target.
The contract requires whole-presentation profiles and explicitly preserves layout-neutral product capabilities, authorization, and active task state.
The contract defines workbench and studio as semantic current identities and contains no numbered, versioned, legacy, or compatibility plan structure.

goal: Revalidate repository gaps and primary framework practices behind the layout design.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Evidence.md` plus current shell, appearance, controller, preference, settings, tests, architecture verifier, product docs, and official Flutter/first-party workbench references. Context: direct IDs, uncoordinated writes, asynchronous hydration, feature-level branches, a fixed mobile shell, and contradictory design text are observable in the working tree. Target: keep every major requirement and architecture choice tied to a file, symbol, test gap, user fact, or primary/open-source practice. Design Considerations: distinguish evidence from inference; compare adaptive resolution, state identity, restoration, theme extension, registry, and reset practices. Design Value: evidence prevents a generic plugin-style abstraction and justifies only the patterns that remove observed coupling or races. Constraints & Risks: cite relative repository paths and public sources only; do not record local identity, raw runtime data, conversations, devices, or secrets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Evidence.md traces the current selection, rendering, persistence, theme, mobile, test, and verifier paths with observed gaps.
Primary Flutter sources support adaptive constraint resolution, state ownership/restoration, ThemeExtension composition, and bounded widget work.

Contradictory documentation, the missing coverage command, dirty-worktree constraint, and seven pre-existing sibling-plan validation issues are recorded without being reclassified as layout deliverables.

goal: Finalize the requirement-to-evidence matrix before layout code changes begin.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Validation.md`, planned layout contract/manager/store/widget tests, architecture checks, Better Plan checks, and existing client commands. Context: current tests prove static shell shapes but not live switching, atomicity, recovery, state continuity, full destination coverage, visual difference, or mobile behavior. Target: map every LAY requirement to deterministic foundation evidence and named desktop/mobile child evidence. Design Considerations: separate unit, widget, golden, integration, build, launch, and authorized-device claims; establish a real coverage command before using coverage as evidence. Design Value: agreeing on proof before implementation prevents easy structural tests from replacing product behavior. Constraints & Risks: aggregate `client:verify` has runtime-data side effects and requires later explicit authorization; store/channel publication is not layout validation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validation.md maps all fourteen requirements to concrete foundation and child-plan evidence.
The matrix covers registry, transaction, corruption, concurrency, destination parity, adaptive resize, state/focus continuity, accessibility, goldens, integration, architecture, build, and launch.
Every listed current command exists; any planned coverage or layout-integration command is explicitly identified as work to establish rather than existing evidence.

goal: Lock the module map, contracts, state machine, data structures, patterns, and child-plan boundaries.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Architecture.md` and initial directories/interfaces under contracts/presentation, application/features/layout, platform/presentation, frontend/layout, and profile variants. Context: one string and direct widget conditions cannot scale to full presentation systems, while an unconstrained plugin framework would exceed the product need. Target: establish inward dependencies, one responsibility per module, registry/factory and strategy boundaries, the preview/commit state machine, typed preference repository, semantic destination coverage, ThemeExtension composition, bounded restoration, and desktop/mobile ownership. Design Considerations: immutable O(1) maps, O(P×V×D) startup validation, one active resolution cache, serialized writes, one active widget tree, and complete-removal rules. Design Value: the selected patterns directly remove branch leakage, stale writes, hidden routes, theme duplication, and state loss. Constraints & Risks: child renderers must not be imported by the parent; no service locator, codegen layer, remote code, versioned directory, or long-lived compatibility path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md records the module/file map, responsibility boundaries, dependency direction, interface contracts, state machine, algorithms, and complexity.
Registry/Factory, Strategy, State Machine/Command, Repository, and ThemeExtension choices are justified against simpler alternatives; deliberately simple areas stay pattern-free.
Desktop and mobile child plans own disjoint variant modules and their architecture criteria verify the parent contract before implementation.
Initial scaffold compiles without moving business logic into frontend profile modules.

goal: Implement pure presentation contracts and one canonical semantic destination catalog.
description: Scope: `apps/desktop/lib/src/contracts/presentation/*.dart`, `application/features/navigation/semantic_destination_catalog.dart`, localized metadata keys, and focused tests. Context: destination lists and aliases are distributed across models, shell navigation, search, README text, and source-string verifiers. Target: immutable profile/environment/selection/preferences/destination values and one exact current destination authority consumed through declared interfaces. Design Considerations: enum/value identities remain semantic; aliases resolve before layout composition; sets/maps use deterministic ordering for tests; contracts import no implementation layer. Design Value: one semantic catalog lets every layout prove equivalent reachability without duplicating navigation policy. Constraints & Risks: preserve current section behavior and capability filtering; do not add feature availability or server policy to presentation descriptors.

acceptance_criteria.text: Contract tests prove immutable parsing/validation, semantic names, deterministic equality/order, viewport classification inputs, and safe error codes.
The destination catalog exactly represents current reachable client surfaces and aliases without importing frontend/platform/backend implementations.
No duplicate shell module list is introduced in the new layout modules.

commit.message: feat(client): add layout and destination contracts

goal: Implement the immutable profile catalog, exact-set validator, adaptive resolver, and bounded presentation-state store.
description: Scope: `application/features/layout/layout_catalog.dart`, `layout_resolver.dart`, `layout_state_store.dart`, and focused unit tests. Context: `ShellLayoutIds.all` performs a linear membership check and carries no coverage, default uniqueness, viewport, or state-boundary contract. Target: one immutable map keyed by profile ID, cached ordered metadata, deterministic catalog validation, O(1) active resolution, and bounded presentation-only state keyed by registered profile/destination/surface. Design Considerations: validate once per catalog revision in O(P×V×D); cache only the active resolution tuple; fail registration rather than falling back across profiles for a missing destination. Design Value: map lookup and exact-set validation prevent branch scans and incomplete layouts while keeping runtime cost constant. Constraints & Risks: no unbounded LRU is needed because valid keys are catalog-bounded; state values cannot contain business data, conversation content, paths, or secrets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Catalog tests reject duplicate IDs, missing/duplicate defaults, numbered identities, incomplete viewport or destination coverage, and mismatched revisions.
Resolver tests prove stable selected identity across resize, deterministic default recovery, and O(1) map-based active lookup without catalog scans in build paths.
Presentation-state tests prove valid-key bounds, per-profile isolation, deterministic reset, and rejection of unregistered keys.

commit.message: feat(client): add deterministic layout catalog and resolver

goal: Implement transactional presentation preferences and the preview/commit layout manager.
description: Scope: `contracts/presentation/presentation_preferences.dart`, `platform/presentation/presentation_preferences_repository.dart`, `application/features/layout/layout_manager.dart`, controller composition, startup hydration, and tests. Context: three uncoordinated read-modify-write setters can lose fields; layout UI is notified before persistence succeeds; non-default startup can flash the default shell. Target: one typed canonical preference document, serialized atomic commits, loading/stable/previewing/committing/error states, monotonic operation epochs, confirm/cancel/reset, deterministic default recovery, and first-shell hydration. Design Considerations: preview is memory-only; confirm persists before promotion; stale completions cannot win; safe errors are bounded codes; appearance catalog loading remains separate. Design Value: the transaction converts a race-prone mutable string into an auditable user action with rollback. Constraints & Risks: ignore and remove the retired `shellLayoutId` field rather than dual-reading it; preserve appearance and locale values; do not log raw documents or local paths.

acceptance_criteria.text: Repository tests prove serialized concurrent layout/appearance/locale updates, atomic replacement, canonical output, corrupt-file recovery, and no retired field on write.
Manager tests prove initialize, preview, confirm, cancel, reset, timeout, invalid/unavailable ID, save failure rollback, and stale-operation suppression.
The first meaningful shell waits for preference hydration and failures expose only a localized safe error state.
ClientController no longer owns a second mutable layout string or independent layout preference setter.

goal: Implement the single frontend layout host, typed widget registry, visual-token composition, focus continuity, and architecture gates.
description: Scope: `frontend/layout/layout_definition.dart`, `layout_registry.dart`, `layout_host.dart`, `layout_visual_tokens.dart`, `layout_component_kit.dart`, `layout_focus_coordinator.dart`, `lib/app.dart`, theme composition, architecture verifier, and focused tests. Context: current ID checks sit in shell and feature code, appearance owns only colors, and root replacement can discard focus/local state. Target: one widget registry matching the pure catalog, one active layout host, ThemeExtension-based non-color tokens, semantic focus capture/restore, stable restoration keys, reduced-motion-safe switching, and verifier rules that ban profile branches elsewhere. Design Considerations: builders are frontend-only; only genuinely different component roles use a kit; const/shared leaf widgets remain simple; `ValueKey(profileId)` identifies a switch and transitions cannot accumulate outgoing trees. Design Value: the host centralizes variation while keeping feature logic testable and preventing a profile matrix from infecting every page. Constraints & Risks: do not keep every profile alive, use whole-tree GlobalKeys, or add a runtime layout plugin loader; child variant definitions remain in child-owned files.

acceptance_criteria.text: Frontend registry tests prove exact ID parity with the pure catalog, exact destination/viewport builders, one default, and deterministic previews.
Theme tests compose every built-in appearance palette with both layout token families without resetting the appearance selection.
Focus/restoration tests prove semantic restoration without a whole-tree GlobalKey or permanently mounted inactive profiles.
Architecture verification forbids profile-ID checks outside registration/tests and validates destination coverage through structure rather than source-string placement.

commit.message: feat(client): centralize profile rendering in layout host

goal: Prove the platform-neutral layout foundation and hand stable contracts to both renderer child plans.
description: Scope: all foundation files, mapped tests from `Validation.md`, architecture/plan/contracts gates, plan-scoped manifest validation, label traceability, and child architecture contract checks. Context: foundation completion is not a claim that desktop/mobile renderers or public releases are complete; it proves the shared authority they consume. Target: run the deterministic foundation matrix, confirm no retired layout selection path remains, and verify both child plans reference the current contracts and can own disjoint renderer files. Design Considerations: evidence should be command/file-backed and privacy-minimal; full `client:verify` requires explicit side-effect authorization. Design Value: a separate foundation receipt makes platform branches independently reviewable without duplicating selection and persistence logic. Constraints & Risks: do not claim full-workspace Better Plan closure while the seven pre-existing sibling issues remain; do not mark child renderer requirements complete from foundation tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: All foundation unit/widget/architecture checks mapped in Validation.md pass with command or file evidence.
Static evidence proves ShellLayoutIds, shellLayoutId, old preference read/write methods, numbered layout labels, and direct profile branches are absent from current implementation paths.
npm run client:format:check, client:analyze, client:test, client:verify:architecture, client:verify:plan, and client:contracts:test pass.
Scoped Better Plan validate --check-sources and check-labels pass for layout-management, and desktop/mobile child architecture criteria resolve against the same current contract files.
